facts.content: Patient's chief complaint is watery diarrhoea for three days.
facts.source_text: Watery diarrhoea for three days.

facts.content: 27-year-old man has had profuse watery diarrhoea for three days, approximately hourly while awake.
facts.source_text: 27-year-old man with 3-day history of profuse watery diarrhoea (≈ hourly while awake).

facts.content: He experiences intermittent crampy mid-lower abdominal pain rated about 6 out of 10 that precedes each stool.
facts.source_text: Associated crampy mid-lower abdominal pain, intermittent, ~6/10, precedes each stool.

facts.content: He has nausea and occasional vomiting, especially after ingesting milk.
facts.source_text: Nausea and occasional vomiting, especially after milk ingestion.

facts.content: Patient reports a subjective fever described as feeling really hot without a recorded temperature.
facts.source_text: Subjective fever (“feeling really hot”) but no recorded temperature.

facts.content: He denies visible blood in the stool.
facts.source_text: Denies visible blood in stool.

facts.content: He reports slightly decreased urinary frequency.
facts.source_text: Reports slightly decreased urine frequency.

facts.content: No known precipitating food was identified and his brother has had a similar illness for five days and is improving.
facts.source_text: No known precipitating food; brother has had similar illness × 5 days and is improving.

facts.content: He has had no prior similar episodes.
facts.source_text: No prior similar episodes.

facts.content: Review of systems positive for watery diarrhoea.
facts.source_text: + watery diarrhoea

facts.content: Review of systems positive for abdominal cramps.
facts.source_text: + abdominal cramps

facts.content: Review of systems positive for nausea and vomiting.
facts.source_text: + nausea/vomiting

facts.content: Review of systems negative for haematochezia.
facts.source_text: – haematochezia

facts.content: Review of systems positive for subjective fever.
facts.source_text: + subjective fever

facts.content: Review of systems negative for weight loss.
facts.source_text: – weight loss (not asked)

facts.content: Review of systems positive for mildly decreased urine frequency.
facts.source_text: + mildly decreased urine frequency

facts.content: Patient reports no chronic medical illnesses and describes himself as fit and well.
facts.source_text: “Fit and well” – no chronic illnesses reported.

facts.content: Patient takes paracetamol as needed for pain or fever; dose and frequency not documented.
facts.source_text: Paracetamol (acetaminophen) – dose/route/frequency not documented, taken PRN for pain/fever.

facts.content: He takes no regular prescription medications.
facts.source_text: No regular prescription medications.

facts.content: Patient has no known drug allergies.
facts.source_text: No known drug allergies.

facts.content: Patient's father had stage III colorectal cancer.
facts.source_text: Father: colorectal cancer, stage III (details unknown).

facts.content: Patient's brother recently experienced a similar self-resolving diarrhoeal illness.
facts.source_text: Brother: recent similar diarrhoeal illness (self-resolving).

facts.content: Patient lives with his mother and sister.
facts.source_text: Lives with mother and sister.

facts.content: He works in a government office in Central London.
facts.source_text: Employment: Government office worker in Central London.

facts.content: He smokes cigarettes socially about once weekly, mainly on Fridays.
facts.source_text: Tobacco: Occasional social cigarette use (≈ once weekly, mainly Fridays).

facts.content: He drinks alcohol occasionally, typically one beer on weekdays and heavier intake one to two times per month with friends.
facts.source_text: Alcohol: Occasional; 1 beer on weekdays, heavier intake 1–2 ×/month with friends.

facts.content: Primary impression is acute gastroenteritis likely infectious and probably viral.
facts.source_text: Acute gastroenteritis, likely infectious (probable viral given household contact, rapid onset, watery stool).

facts.content: Differential diagnosis includes bacterial gastroenteritis.
facts.source_text: bacterial gastroenteritis

facts.content: Differential diagnosis includes lactose intolerance or exacerbation.
facts.source_text: lactose intolerance/exacerbation

facts.content: Differential diagnosis includes early inflammatory bowel disease.
facts.source_text: early inflammatory bowel disease

facts.content: Differential diagnosis includes food-borne toxin–mediated illness.
facts.source_text: food-borne toxin–mediated illness

facts.content: Patient is currently at mild to moderate risk of dehydration.
facts.source_text: Currently mild-moderate dehydration risk (profuse stool output, subjective fever, ↓ urine).

facts.content: Begin oral rehydration solution such as Dioralyte and maintain high oral fluid intake.
facts.source_text: Oral rehydration: Begin oral rehydration solution (ORS) such as Dioralyte; maintain high oral fluid intake.

facts.content: Follow a clear fluids then bland soft diet and avoid dairy and alcohol until recovery.
facts.source_text: Diet: Clear fluids then bland/soft diet (soup, mashed foods); avoid dairy and alcohol until recovery.

facts.content: Continue paracetamol as needed for pain or fever per package instructions.
facts.source_text: Symptom control: Continue paracetamol as needed for pain/fever (dose per package instructions).

facts.content: Patient educated on signs of dehydration and red-flag symptoms such as blood in stool or persistent vomiting.
facts.source_text: Education: Discussed signs of dehydration (dizziness, minimal urine, persistent fever) and red-flag symptoms (blood in stool, worsening pain, persistent vomiting).

facts.content: If no improvement or worsening occurs within 48 hours or if he cannot maintain hydration, he should contact the clinic or emergency department for further evaluation.
facts.source_text: Safety-netting: If no improvement or worsening within 48 h, or inability to maintain hydration, contact clinic/ED for further evaluation (consider labs, stool studies, IV fluids).

facts.content: Disposition is home with self-care and strict return precautions.
facts.source_text: Disposition: Home with self-care and strict return precautions.

facts.content: A telephone review is planned in one to two days if symptoms persist or sooner if concerned.
facts.source_text: Follow-up: Telephone review in 1–2 days if symptoms persist or sooner if concerned.
